subject: In-flight backpressure failure + websocket timeouts — urgent customer escalation

Cc: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@clearpath.ai>

Subject: Live inference — sustained silent chunks and timeouts since 08:50 PT

Ethan —

We started seeing the problem again this morning during a high-throughput batch of patient summarizations. Between 08:50 and 09:05 PT ~40% of requests either stalled (no token chunks for 8–12s) or returned a WebSocket 504. Throughput dropped by about 30% and latency spiked to 4–5s for the remainder.

Attached two artifacts: a screenshot of the chunk timeline and the log bundle from our proxy. We did a quick smoke and the downstream consumer saw partial payloads that never finished. This is P1 for our ops team — impact on scheduled workflows.

Can you confirm this is on Redwood side and advise immediate mitigation/fallback? We have a weekly EHR ingestion window at 09:15 PT and cannot afford repeated failures.

Thanks,
Oliver
Sr. Platform Engineer
Acme Health

Oliver —

Thanks for the quick report and artifacts. I've looped in Marissa from Customer Success for runbook/action and Neha from SRE for an engineering triage. Marissa: can your ops team validate whether the requests that timed out hit our edge or errored from upstream? Neha: can you review the attached traces and look for backpressure signals (queue growth on the serving proxies) or kernel-level stalls?

Immediate proposal: 1) failover the tenant to a lower-concurrency/pinned model variant for the next 30m, 2) enable aggressive keepalive and reduce idle socket timeout at the proxy layer, 3) capture a full pcap + request/response timings. If agreed I'll push the failover now.

Oliver / Ethan —

We ran quick verification against Acme's tenant metrics. Observations:
- At ~08:48 PT we see a sharp increase in queued requests at the proxy (x2 of baseline) with a sustained elevated queue for ~12 minutes.
- Token output rate shows intermittent 6–10s gaps for a subset of streams (matches your screenshot).
- Error-rate for WS 504s climbed to 7.2% during the window (baseline ~0.3%).

Immediate actions taken:
- Flipped routing policy to the pinned small-rt variant (low-concurrency) at 09:00 PT — dropped error-rate to 1.1% but throughput is lower.
- Captured request logs and packaged (redwood-request-logs-20261010.txt) — attached.

Next: Neha will validate kernel and GPU-side backpressure metrics. Jordan, flag this for the renewal exec touchpoint — Acme is sensitive to outages during ingestion windows.

—Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Live inference — sustained silent chunks and timeouts since 08:50 PT

Team — preliminary triage:
- Kernel-level scheduling looked normal; no OOMs.
- Serving runtime shows repeated KV-cache thrashing for some long-sequence requests (high prefix reuse) which produces CPU spikes on the proxy tier and stalls token emission while rehydrating caches.
- We also saw a cascade where continuous batching exceeded the configured batch-duration threshold for the small-rt variant under this sequence distribution — leading to per-request stall windows.

Hypothesis: a workload change (higher sequence length + prefix similarity) produced backpressure at the proxy/batching boundary. When batching waits to aggregate other requests, the long-running rehydration briefly blocks emission of earlier tokens, causing the visible 6–12s silent spans and eventual socket timeouts.

Action items I recommend:
1) Keep the tenant on the pinned small-rt variant (we did).
2) Temporarily prioritize token emission (reduce max-batch-duration to 10ms for this tenant) — low risk, restores latency at cost of throughput.
3) Ship a targeted hotfix to improve KV-cache rehydration concurrency within 48 hours.

I'll start a runbook and open INF-4821 with logs attached. Neha
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
